While not directly related to R (but R can be used in this class for some parts) I think this may be of interest to those who came to the mapping talks.

Geo 290: Cartography
Spring Quarter
Units: 2
CRN: 53930

Lecture: Tuesdays 9:00-10:00 Wellman 3
Lab: Tuesdays 2:00-5:00 Hunt 253

Instructor: Michele Tobias, geospatial scientist at Geospatial Consulting @ UC Davis & GGG alumna

Course Description: This course is designed to introduce students to principles of cartography through theoretical and applied approaches.
Students will explore the history of cartography and various map projections, and will be exposed to methodologies and software used in creating thematic representations of the world. Topics include standards of map design, data acquisition and representation and ethics in mapping.

Prerequisites: Introductory GIS course (LDA 150 or similar) & graduate standing (or permission of the instructor)

Questions:mmto...@ucdavis.edu

This course is not scheduled to be taught regularly. You are encouraged to take the course now if you interested as it may not be taught again for several years. It was last taught in 2010.
